podcast.body: Featured on the 1978 album *Hemispheres*, this was Rush's first purely instrumental piece and is composed of 12 distinct movements. The song originated from a dream that guitarist Alex Lifeson had. Its recording was an extensive process, reportedly taking longer to complete than the entire *Fly By Night* album. "One of the greatest Rush instruments of all time is La Villa Strangato from 1978's Hemispheres."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This long, multi-movement instrumental from their album Hemispheres includes two sections titled "Monsters." These sections were found to be similar to a 1937 jazz piece by Raymond Scott, resulting in a legal issue and financial cost for Rush, who had mistakenly believed the older piece was in the public domain. "It's a long, multi-movement instrumental which contains two sections entitled Monsters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
